units.passage: The instructor may provide additional instructions or limits for any authorized activity. Permitted Actions You may use AI for general questions and support–including concept explanations, study questions, practice problems, ungraded exercises, and exploratory coding–on all work. You may use AI to help develop your submissions only for the specific assignments listed in Authorized Graded Work , subject to any instructions or limits stated for that activity. Prohibited Actions Do not use AI to produce work you submit on any graded assignment that is not listed under Authorized Graded Work . Do not use AI in ways that exceed the stated limits for an authorized graded activity. Do not submit AI-generated work, or lightly edited AI-generated work, as your own when the activity's instructions require work to be independently produced. If an assignment has stricter rules, those rules override this policy for that assignment. Examples Allowed: using AI to explain a concept, generate practice questions, or help you study for a quiz. Allowed: using AI on an ungraded practice exercise or exploratory code that will not be submitted for credit. units.passage: You ARE allowed to use ChatGPT, Google Bard, Bing AI, or similar AI chatbots as you would a library resource. For example, you can use ChatGPT to find solutions for errors the same way you would use Stackoverflow or other Internet resources, or to understand and improve software you are developing. You ARE allowed to use AI chatbots to verify algorithms. You will learn more if you develop your algorithms yourself and use a chatbot to verify them, rather than taking the shortcut of simply (for example) asking ChatGPT to generate the algorithms for you. In fact, you'll learn more about both the problem you are trying to solve and the critical thinking skills that AI cannot replace. In your career, there are guaranteed to be problems for which AI cannot propose algorithms or solutions. If you have not developed the critical thinking skills to develop solution algorithms on your own, you will be unable to deliver the value your employer expects from a practicing engineer. You ARE allowed to use AI chatbots for small snippets of code, as you would by using online reference like Reddit or a language-specific website that helps engineers understand how to implement certain tasks in different programming languages.
